correctness.rationale: The separable Spin(4) double cover is established by quaternion norm multiplicativity, its order-two kernel, full dimension and invertible characteristic. The diagonal Hadamard identity is checked exactly. At every point the nonzero supports are disjoint and nonempty; two norm constraints eliminate by invertible partial derivatives, leaving r=0,1,2 independent equations x_i y_i=0. Thus the three completed rings are exhaustive; each is reduced Gorenstein and has multiplicity 2^r. The Jacobian Fitting ideal is (x,y) for r=1 and all six pairwise products for r=2, proving reducedness. All support configurations are counted explicitly; standalone checker returned HSO4_EXACT_CHECK_OK. No finite test is substituted for the uniform proof.

value.rationale: The motivating hollow SO(4) slice has a published combinatorial incidence decomposition but no scheme-theoretic classification of its transverse contacts. Exact completed local rings and reduced Fitting singular schemes decide geometric crossing versus tangency, determine three Hilbert--Samuel multiplicities and detect 24 genuine two-node product points. This structural information is needed for local intersection/deformation calculations and cannot be read from a component count, making it materially more than a routine repackaging of an incidence table. It does not claim a new general theorem about all orthogonal slices.
